questions.text: Meta-prompting replaces prompt engineering: once you can hold a planning dialogue with the AI, writing a specific, well-structured prompt is no longer necessary.
questions.explanation: The lesson is explicit that meta-prompting is a preliminary step, not a replacement. First you use it to clarify what you want; then you write a specific prompt to get it, as the worked Year 3 example demonstrates.

questions.text: What does the lesson describe as Meta-prompting 1.0?

options.text: Presenting a draft prompt to the AI and asking how it could be improved before submitting it as a task.
Beginning with no prompt at all and exploring possible approaches through dialogue.
Asking the AI to assess the quality of the output it has just produced.
Writing several versions of the same prompt and comparing the results side by side.

questions.explanation: Meta-prompting 1.0 is the simplest form: you show the AI your draft and ask what is missing. Starting from a problem rather than a prompt and exploring options through conversation is the more advanced form, Meta-prompting 2.0.

questions.text: In which situations does the lesson say meta-prompting is most valuable?

options.text: When you know the problem but not what form the solution should take.
When a complex task has several components and the structure needs planning before content is generated.
When you want to weigh up different approaches before committing to one.
When the task is simple and well defined, such as ten exercises on the 6 times table.
When you want a single finished product and no further conversation.

questions.explanation: The lesson lists exploring the form of a solution, planning a multi-part task and evaluating alternatives among the situations where meta-prompting pays off. For a simple, well-defined request it says meta-prompting is unnecessary, and it contrasts the collaborative mode with the one-shot transactional one.

questions.text: What role does the AI play during a meta-prompting conversation?

options.text: It presents options, structures and possibilities that the teacher accepts, rejects or modifies using professional judgement.
It selects the most pedagogically appropriate option, which the teacher then implements.
It takes over the planning stage so the teacher can move straight to delivery.
It stores the teacher's preferences so that later prompts become unnecessary.

questions.explanation: The lesson states that the AI is not making decisions in a meta-prompting conversation — it offers possibilities, and the teacher's expertise is exercised in evaluating them and steering the dialogue towards a useful outcome.
